messages.author: 7ac73294c2aec102
messages.subject: predict function and occuMulti error
parts:
I've run into a brick wall that I can't seem to figure my way out of, so I was hoping that someone might be able to give me a hand.  It is probably something really simple that I'm just not seeing, and I hope that's the case!

I am using the occuMulti function to fit multispecies occupancy models.  My candidate model set is 46 models, with 3 continuous covariates for occupancy and no detection covariates.  There are 90 sites that were surveyed 24 times.  I am trying to make model averaged predictions using the predict function but I keep getting an error (I am able to get model-averaged estimates using modavg, so that's helpful).  

Here's the code:

#List of fitted models
fl <- fitList(fit2,fit3,fit4,fit5,fit6,fit7,fit8,fit9,fit10,fit11,fit12,fit13,fit14,fit15,fit16,fit17,
              fit18,fit19,fit20,fit21,fit22,fit23,fit24,fit25,fit26,fit27,fit28,fit29,fit30,fit31,fit32,
              fit33,fit34,fit35,fit36,fit37,fit38,fit39,fit40,fit41,fit42,fit43,fit44,fit45,fit46,fit47)

#new data for predictions
newdune <- newwet <- newroad <- scale(c(0,10,20,30,40,50,100,250,500,1000))
new.dat <- data.frame(Dune=newdune, Wetland=newwet, Road=newroad) 

# Model-averaged predictions
predict(fl, type="state", new.dat)

Here's the error:
Error in x[, "Predicted"] : incorrect number of dimensions

I thought maybe the length of the new data needed to = that of the original (90 sites), so I tried this:
newdune <- newwet <- newroad <- scale(rep(c(0,10,20,30,40,50,100,250,500,1000),9))

But I get the same error.

Any thoughts would be much appreciated!!! Thank you!

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: predict function and occuMulti error
parts:
It's not you - I just haven't implemented a way to handle predicting from occuMulti fitLists (yet), sorry!

For most types of unmarked models it just works, but since occuMulti returns some more complex output from predict it breaks and has to be handled in a different way. Until then you would have to calculate the predictions from the modavg output manually. I have an idea for a temporary workaround - will update later if it works.

Ken

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: predict function and occuMulti error
parts:
Hi Michelle,

To get your model-averaged predictions manually, you can make your
predictions for each model separately, then use modavgCustom( ) by
supplying a vector of log-likelihoods, K, model names, predictions,
SE's. The trick with modavgCustom( ) is to make your predictions from
your data frame one row at a time. 

This could be implemented in a loop or apply functions. For example,
using the example in ?occuMulti, if you wanted to model-average the
marginal occupancy of bear, you could proceed as follows:

##continuing example ?occuMulti
##assemble models in list
modList <- list("fit" = fit, "fit2" = fit2, "fit3" = fit3)

## 1) predict "bear" marginal occupancy across each model
bearFit <- predict(fit, type = "state", species = "bear")
bearFit2 <- predict(fit2, type = "state", species = "bear") 
bearFit3 <- predict(fit3, type = "state", species = "bear")

##assemble in list
bearList <- list(bearFit, bearFit2, bearFit3)

##extract logL and K
logL <- sapply(modList, logLik)
K <- sapply(modList, AICc, return.K = TRUE)

## 2) iterate over each row to model average
nRows <- nrow(bear.fit)
predsModAvg <- matrix(NA, nrow = nRows, ncol = 4)
colnames(predsModAvg) <- c("pred", "se",
                           "low95", "upp95")
    for (i in 1:nRows) {

        ##extract preds and SE's
        predRows <- sapply(bearList, FUN = function(x) x[i,  
"Predicted"])
        seRows <- sapply(bearList, FUN = function(x) x[i, "SE"])

        ##model-average predictions
        modAvgRows <- modavgCustom(logL = logL, K = K,
                                   modnames = names(modList),
                                   estimat = predRows,
                                   se = seRows,
                                   second.ord = FALSE)
        ##store in results matrix
        predsModAvg[i, "pred"] <- modAvgRows$Mod.avg.est
        predsModAvg[i, "se"] <- modAvgRows$Uncond.SE
        predsModAvg[i, "low95"] <- modAvgRows$Lower.CL
        predsModAvg[i, "upp95"] <- modAvgRows$Upper.CL
    }

head(predsModAvg)


Note that the predict method for fitList objects in unmarked uses the
"old" equation of the unconditional SE of Burnham and Anderson, whereas
modavgCustom( ) and other functions in AICcmodavg use the revised
equation. This explains the slight discrepancy in unconditional SE's.
See details on the uncond.se argument in ?modavgCustom.


Hope it helps,

Marc
